description_full: SEEK Limited, together with its subsidiaries, provides online employment marketplace services in Australia, New Zealand, Southeast Asia, Hong Kong, the United Kingdom, Europe, and internationally. The company's job advertisement solutions include Lite ad, which is a free ad designed for non-urgent; Basic ad, which offers search visibility and candidate recommendations; Advanced ad, which offers increased search visibility and AI candidate targeting for specialized or competitive roles; and Premium ad for business-critical or time-sensitive roles. It also offers sourcing solutions, such as Talent Search, which allows hirers to search candidate database; SEEK Pass that helps candidates stand out by verifying credentials on their application and profile, as well as helping hirers assess candidates; Employer Brand Boost, which allows hirers to amplify their employee value proposition; SEEKGrad that assists employers with early-career and graduate recruitment; JobAdder, which serves as an applicant tracking system and customer management platform for recruiters and talent acquisition teams; Sidekicker that serves as a labour marketplace providing on-demand labour across hospitality, events, retail, customer service, aged care, warehousing, and logistics industries. In addition, the company offers HR software as a service (SaaS) and ad enhancements. SEEK Limited was incorporated in 1997 and is headquartered in Melbourne, Australia.

financial_summary: SEEK LIMITED is a mid-cap communication services business with a $3.5B market cap on $870M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +2% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are contracting by -2.8pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 7% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically. Gross margins of 100% confirm genuine pricing power.
The business throws off $167M in free cash flow — roughly 19 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.7× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 4.4×.

Shareholder yield of 3.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 10% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
